- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often over-anticipates decline; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean or adjust downward to match recent low.
- Model frequently over-responds to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) with overshoot in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or apply decay factor.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, model often fails to revert; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day after peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period volatility (especially after sentiment shifts); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment turns bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3–5 day highs/lows; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment is volatile or noisy.
